say: First, density: how many strands grow on the scalp. Make a part at the crown, hairline, temples and nape, and see how much scalp shows. Temples are often thinnest.

panel.heading: Four checks with your hands
items: Density: part at crown, hairline, temples, nape
Strand width: a shed hair next to sewing thread
Porosity: spray water and watch it
Elasticity: gently stretch one wet strand

say: Second, strand width. Hold a shed hair next to sewing thread. Thinner than the thread is fine hair, which breaks easily and needs less added weight.

panel.heading: Four checks with your hands
items: Density: part at crown, hairline, temples, nape
Strand width: a shed hair next to sewing thread
Porosity: spray water and watch it
Elasticity: gently stretch one wet strand

say: Third, porosity: how water gets in and out. If sprayed water sits in droplets and dries slowly, porosity is low. If it soaks in and dries fast, it is high.

panel.heading: Four checks with your hands
items: Density: part at crown, hairline, temples, nape
Strand width: a shed hair next to sewing thread
Porosity: spray water and watch it
Elasticity: gently stretch one wet strand

say: Fourth, elasticity. Do every check in daylight or with a phone torch, because dim light hides thin temples.

panel.heading: Four checks with your hands
items: Density: part at crown, hairline, temples, nape
Strand width: a shed hair next to sewing thread
Porosity: spray water and watch it
Elasticity: gently stretch one wet strand

say: Step 1. Take one wet strand from the back of the head.

panel.heading: The elasticity test
items: Take one wet strand from the back of the head
Hold it firmly near the root
Stretch slowly and gently, then release
Write the result on her card

say: Step 2. Hold it firmly near the root, so you do not pull her scalp.

panel.heading: The elasticity test
items: Take one wet strand from the back of the head
Hold it firmly near the root
Stretch slowly and gently, then release
Write the result on her card

say: Step 3. Stretch it slowly and gently, then let go. Healthy hair springs back. Hair that snaps at once is brittle. Hair that stays stretched and gummy is weak.

panel.heading: The elasticity test
items: Take one wet strand from the back of the head
Hold it firmly near the root
Stretch slowly and gently, then release
Write the result on her card

say: Step 4. Write the result on her card, and never repeat the test on the same strand.

panel.heading: The elasticity test
items: Take one wet strand from the back of the head
Hold it firmly near the root
Stretch slowly and gently, then release
Write the result on her card

say: For example, Amaka in Enugu has a client, Funmi, who wants small waist-length knotless braids for a wedding. Funmi's hair is fine, with thin temples.

panel.heading: From findings to a safer style
right: Temple hair with no added hair

say: So Amaka recommends medium knotless braids at mid-back length, with no added hair at the temples, and extra drying time because the hair has low porosity. Funmi still gets her braids, in a size her hair can carry.

panel.heading: From findings to a safer style
right: Temple hair with no added hair

say: Check the scalp in good light before you wet or comb. Light white flakes with no redness or pain? Serve, and note it on her card.

cards.d: Light white flakes, no redness, no pain. Cleanse gently and note it on her card.
Lice or nits, round scaly patches with broken hairs, pus or sores. Do not serve today.
Thin edges: no tension there. Cuts or raw skin: no chemicals, and do not braid over it.

say: Lice or eggs, round scaly patches with broken hairs, pus or sores? Do not serve today. Tell her privately what you saw and suggest a health worker. Never diagnose.

say: Thin edges mean no tension there. Raw skin means no chemicals and no braiding over it. Wear disposable gloves near broken skin.

say: Afterwards, bag every comb, clip and towel you touched.

panel.heading: After a problem scalp
items: Bag every comb, clip and towel you touched
Lice: soak combs in water of at least about 54°C
Fungal signs: wash with soap, then disinfect
Wash your hands for 40 to 60 seconds

say: For lice, soak combs in hot water of at least about 54 degrees Celsius for 5 to 10 minutes.

say: For fungal signs, wash with soap and water, then disinfect as you will learn in module 4.

say: Wash your hands for 40 to 60 seconds. And never give medicine or treat a scalp yourself.

panel.rule: Never give medicine or apply any treatment. Stop, protect, refer.

say: For example, Chioma in Onitsha plans medium knotless braids: 8 rows of about 10 braids makes 80 braids.

panel.heading: Quote the time before you start
items: 8 rows x 10 braids = 80 braids
80 braids x 6 minutes = 480 minutes
Add 30 minutes wash, 60 minutes drying
Total 570 minutes: 9 hours 30 minutes

say: Her own timed average is 6 minutes per braid, so that is 480 minutes.

say: Keep a private card for every visit: her details, your checks, her history, the agreed style, time, price, deposit, and photo consent. For a child, the parent agrees.
Read it back and ask her to reply agreed on WhatsApp.

panel.heading: Fill in her record card
items: Name and the phone number she agrees to share
Assessment and scalp check results
Past styles, relaxer or colour, sensitivities
Agreed style, size, length and who brings hair
Time, price and deposit paid
Photo consent, and parent's agreement for a child

say: To remember. Do the four checks every visit, because hair changes. Fine hair and thin edges need less weight. Postpone and refer privately. Clean every tool. And put time and price in writing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check density, width, porosity and elasticity
Fine hair and thin edges: bigger sections, less weight
Postpone and refer; describe privately, never diagnose
Bag and clean every tool that touched a problem scalp
Quote time from your own averages, in writing
